notes: Seattle has a city file (Secure Scheduling, $21.30 minimum wage).
No state daily overtime listed in the DOL table.
Drafted from US DOL WHD state tables (confidence=medium) on 2026-11-06; upgrade to primary sources pending.
minimum_wage.effective is the DOL table date (2026-11-05), not the statutory effective date.

Minors (WAC 296-125-101, eff. 2026-07-01): the school-day cap applies to school days preceding another school day, so Friday is 8 h; the validator treats Friday as a school day (stricter). Minors working past 8 p.m. in service jobs need an adult supervisor on site. Extra param key max_days_week.

No tip credit: 'Tips and service charges paid to an employee are in addition to, and may not count towards, the employee's hourly minimum wage' (RCW 49.46.020(3), https://app.leg.wa.gov/RCW/default.aspx?cite=49.46.020). No tipped_minimum_wage rule.

Minor hazardous work (WAC 296-125-131, all minors): mirrors the federal under-18 orders (motor-vehicle driving with the 17-year-old incidental exception, meat-processing machines, bakery machines, balers/compactors, power saws), so federal.json covers them. Under-16 (WAC 296-125-141) is stricter than federal: cooking and baking are banned outright, as is work with or near any power-driven machinery (WA.minor_prohibited_roles.1).

Alcohol (RCW 66.44.340, .350): only 18+ may serve or sell; 18-20s may not bartend or work in bars/lounges beyond passing through for duties, and grocery sales by 18-20s need a 21+ supervisor on duty (two for spirits). Encoded as under-18 alcohol_service (bar-only roles for 18-20 not representable).

rules.summary: During school weeks, minors under 16 may work at most 3 hours on a school day before another school day (8 otherwise), 16 hours and 6 days a week, 7 a.m.-7 p.m. before a school day (9 p.m. Fridays/Saturdays).

citation.title: WAC 296-125-101 — Hours of work for minors (eff. July 1, 2026)
citation.excerpt: A maximum of three hours per day on any school day preceding another school day or otherwise a maximum of eight hours per day; (ii) A maximum of six days per week; (iii) A maximum of 16 hours per week

rules.summary: During non-school weeks, minors under 16 may work at most 8 hours a day, 40 hours and 6 days a week, 7 a.m.-9 p.m.

citation.title: WAC 296-125-101 — Hours of work for minors (eff. July 1, 2026)
citation.excerpt: during nonschool weeks: (i) A maximum of eight hours per day; (ii) A maximum of six days per week; (iii) A maximum of 40 hours per week; (iv) No earlier than 7:00 a.m.; and (v) No later than 9:00 p.m.

rules.summary: During school weeks, 16- and 17-year-olds may work at most 4 hours on a school day before another school day (8 otherwise), 20 hours and 6 days a week, 7 a.m.-10 p.m. before a school day (midnight Fridays/Saturdays).

rules.summary: During non-school weeks, 16- and 17-year-olds may work at most 8 hours a day, 48 hours and 6 days a week, 5 a.m.-midnight.

rules.summary: In Washington minors under 16 may not cook or bake (no federal grill/auto-fryer exception), use ladders or scaffolds, work with or near any power-driven machinery, or drive.

citation.title: WAC 296-125-141 — Prohibited and hazardous employment, special restrictions for minors under 16
citation.excerpt: (5) In occupations involving operation or repair, oiling, cleaning, adjusting, or setting up of or working in proximity to any power-driven machinery. (6) ... motor vehicles ... (8) ... ladders, scaffolds ... (9) ... baking. (10) ... cooking.

params.exception_note: 18-20-year-olds may take orders for, serve and sell liquor in restaurants, clubs, snack bars, caterers and sports venues outside bars/lounges (RCW 66.44.350), and sell/stock in grocery or beer/wine shops with a 21+ supervisor on duty (two for spirits) (RCW 66.44.340).

rules.summary: In Washington, serving or selling alcohol starts at 18: 18-20-year-olds may serve in restaurant dining areas (not bars or lounges) and sell in grocery stores with a 21+ supervisor on duty.

citation.title: RCW 66.44.350 — Employees 18 and over allowed to serve and carry liquor
citation.excerpt: employees ... who are between eighteen and twenty-one years of age may take orders for, serve, and sell liquor in any part of the licensed premises except cocktail lounges, bars, or other areas classified ... off-limits
